findings.where: Screen 12 (Mixed: the eigenvalues), hint for '5 and 2' and the Why
findings.what: "Reading 5 and 2 off the diagonal works only when every entry below it is 0" is false as an absolute, because zeros above the diagonal work as well ([2 0; 5 3] has eigenvalues 2 and 3); say "only when every entry on one side of the diagonal is 0".

findings.where: Whole lesson against the brief's vocabulary list (lesson 5)
findings.what: The brief says this lesson teaches the words "characteristic equation" and "eigenspace", but neither appears on any screen or in the explain; name det(A − λI) = 0 the characteristic equation on screen 5, and call an eigenvector's whole line its eigenspace in screen 2's Why.
It ends "Getting (0, 0) means a slip, often in λ", but here λ = 3 is right, so the slip must be in solving the rows (v₁ is free); say that for this case.

Two steps are skipped on screen: (a − λ)(d − λ) − bc before "multiplies out", and (λ − p)(λ − q) before "it is also λ² − (p + q)λ + pq"; the point, that the eigenvalues add to the trace and multiply to the determinant, also comes after the algebra instead of first.

findings.where: Screen 11 (Three lines in space), SHOW text
findings.what: "Its equation is −λ³ + 4λ² − 3λ = 0" gives no hint of where the equation comes from; adding "Expanding det(C − λI) gives" closes the gap and stays under 90 words, and the full working stays in practice.
"One nonzero row is enough in a 2 by 2" has no reason on screen; add that at an eigenvalue one row is a multiple of the other.

findings.where: Screen 3 (A flip keeps the line), SHOW text
findings.what: The screen carries a second, unrelated idea, that the zero arrow never counts, and its "A0 = λ0" uses A for the mirror while screen 1's A was [3 1; 0 2]; that point fits better in screen 2's or screen 10's Why.

"A matrix on a card, with the probe arrow v and the arrow it becomes below it, or the grid of A − λI" is clumsy ("it becomes below it") and names A − λI before it is defined; something like "A matrix on a card. Below it, an arrow v and the arrow the matrix makes of it." reads better.
Why? opens before Check, and every Why states the answer (screen 13's says "A(2, 1) = (12, 6), which is 6 lots of (2, 1)"), so one tap gives the puzzle away; show Why? only after a Check.

findings.where: Screen 4 (A matrix with no lit line), task
findings.what: "Which preset has no lit line at all?" names a control that will not read in the read-through; give the step a read sentence, for example "Which keeps no line at all: the shear, the quarter turn or the mirror?"

findings.where: All sweep, grid and 3-D pictures, lit and crushed lines
findings.what: Lit and crushed lines are amber, but the brief says an eigenvector line lights "in ink, made bolder, not in a new colour", and CLAUDE.md keeps amber for key terms and what is due; follow the brief, or record that the amber is meant to echo the amber key term "eigenvector".
For the mirror, Av's path is v's circle itself, so the key's "Av's path" swatch has no dashed path to match; label it "Av's path = v's circle" on this screen.
For about the first second the pane shows only the circle and the path, and the arrows fade in at about 1.1 s; start with v drawn so the opening frame shows what moves.
"through v = L di/dt" uses v for voltage in a lesson where v is the eigenvector; write "voltage = L × di/dt".

Apart from the choke analogy, nothing says where eigenvalues earn their keep for an engineer (vibration modes, coupled circuits, control); one sentence pointing ahead to lessons 6 and 7 would give him the payoff.
